newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens to cut jobs in medical equipment.
newsitem.headline: Siemens to cut jobs in medical equipment.

text.p: Siemens AG said it would cut 1,000 jobs as part of a cost-cutting programme in its medical equipment division in 1996/97.
Division chairman Erich Reinhardt said the cost-cutting steps were unavoidable due to deep structural changes in the health-care system and stagnation in the market for medical equipment.
The company would do as much as possible through reductions in overtime and regular working hours, and shifting personnel to other divisions. But some workers might have to be let go, he said.
The division now employes about 22,500 workers, down 5,500 from four years ago, the company said.
"In view of the continued market weakness and sharpening competitive situation, these (previous) measures are not sufficient," Reinhardt said.
The medical systems division had sales of 6.8 billion marks in 1994/95, and pretax profit of 100 million marks.
